package.title: Advance Care Planning: Randomized Trial Evidence on Preference-Sensitive End-of-Life Care and Costs
package.description: Source package for the report: citation metadata, links, short evidence notes and available source files for each study.

folders.papers/: One PDF per study where available. Files ending __rendered_from_PMC.pdf were generated from PMC full-text XML.
folders.fulltext/<ID>/: PMC open-data full text (JATS XML, plain text, figures, supplements, PMC metadata).
folders.registry/: ClinicalTrials.gov records (JSON) and posted protocols, statistical analysis plans and consent forms.
folders.report/: The report exported from the doc (PDF and Markdown).
folders.scripts/: Scripts used to look up citations, collect files and build this package.

field_guide.availability: pdf = publisher or repository PDF; rendered_pmc = PDF rendered from PMC full text; links_only = no free copy could be downloaded
field_guide.effect_on_care: Trials only: effect on preference-sensitive care received (Improved = less burdensome or more preference-concordant care on at least one outcome)

package.licensing: Files keep their original licenses (see license_or_access). CC BY / CC BY-NC items are open access. Items marked 'NIH author manuscript' are free-to-read PMC copies provided for text mining and personal use; do not redistribute them.

studies.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 55 RCTs; pooled gains in directive completion and discussions; communication-based ACP improved preference-care concordance
studies.availability_note: No open-access copy found (checked OpenAlex open-access locations and PMC open data); publisher access required.

studies.title: The effects of advance care planning intervention on nursing home residents: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
studies.authors: Ng AYM, Takemura N, Xu X, Smith R, Kwok JY, Cheung DST, Lin CC.
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 9 nursing-home RCTs (2,905 residents); documentation OR 1.95; family satisfaction no difference; care received not pooled
studies.availability_note: No open-access copy found (checked OpenAlex open-access locations and PMC open data); publisher access required.

studies.title: The Effect of Advance Care Planning on Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
studies.authors: Schichtel M, Wee B, Perera R, Onakpoya I.
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 14 heart failure RCTs (2,924 patients); QoL SMD 0.38, satisfaction 0.39, communication 0.29; care received not pooled

files.source: Journal of General Internal Medicine (publishedVersion, cc-by)
